Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failing test `testNestedWithCommentsJDOM()` calls `doTest` with the "nested-with-comments" XML and the JDOM model. According to the bug report, JXPath automatically trims string values retrieved from XML elements. Inspecting the implementation of `org.apache.commons.jxpath.ri.model.jdom.JDOMNodePointer.getValue()` confirms this: it returns text content using methods that trim whitespace. For example, for an `Element` node, it calls `((Element) node).getTextTrim()`, which trims leading and trailing whitespace. Similarly, for `Comment` and `ProcessingInstruction` nodes, the code explicitly calls `trim()` on the text content before returning it. For `Text` and `CDATA` nodes, it also uses `getTextTrim()`. This behavior causes the XML content to lose leading and trailing spaces when accessed through JXPath, which is contrary to the expectation in the test and bug report. Because `getValue()` is the method responsible for returning node values, its trimming logic is the root cause of the problem. The issue report's expectation is to preserve these spaces, but current implementation aggressively trims them.

Therefore, the fault lies in `JDOMNodePointer.getValue()` method which trims values before returning, causing loss of leading and trailing spaces.

Next step: Fix the `getValue()` method to avoid trimming text nodes so that original whitespace is preserved.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
